posts.text:
I founded the Congressional Childhood Cancer Caucus in 2009 with one goal: to give children with cancer a voice in Washington. Seventeen years later, we've passed several pieces of game-changing legislation, funded hundreds of millions of dollars of research, and dramatically expanded treatment options for these precious children.

Today, we gathered at my 17th annual Childhood Cancer Summit to celebrate our many victories, to remember and honor the legacies of the children we've tragically lost

posts.text:
Today, I introduced the Ailani Myers AIM to Cure Kids With Cancer Act — a bill that would leverage AI to drive pediatric cancer breakthroughs.

The bill is named in honor of Ailani, a precious young cancer fighter who has fiercely advocated for the childhood cancer community. We owe it to children like her to provide the best possible treatments as we work toward beating this heartbreaking disease once and for all.
posts.summary: Advocates AI-driven pediatric cancer research legislation

Lindsey was a mentor and a good friend to me, and I can think of no better tribute to his legacy than today’s bill signing ceremony. 

This bill will give @POTUS tremendous leverage over our adversaries to bring this conflict to a peaceful resolution. 

It was an honor to introduce it in the House and see it across the finish line.
